sections.text:
Noah, peace be upon him, was the first messenger sent by God to the people of the earth after they fell into polytheism and idolatry.

After the death of righteous men from his people (Wad, Suwa, Yaghuth, Ya`uq, and Nisr), Satan pleased them to make statues in memory of them.

As generations passed, people forgot the real reason for making statues, and began to worship them instead of God.

God sent Noah to warn them of a painful punishment if they did not repent and return to worshiping the One, All-Powerful God.

Noah began his call in a gentle and affectionate manner, calling them, saying: “O my people, worship God. You have no god but Him.”

But the people were arrogant and mocked him, and they put their fingers in their ears and covered themselves with their clothes so that they would not hear his words.

Noah did not despair, and continued to invite them day and night, secretly and publicly, and did not leave an opportunity without advising them.

He reminded them of God’s blessings upon them, His creation of the heavens and the earth, and His sending of rain, but their hearts were harder than stones.

A hundred years passed, then two hundred, then three hundred, and Noah was patient, patient, and did not get bored or despair.

His call lasted nine hundred and fifty years! Despite this long life in preaching, only a very few of the weak and poor believed in him.

As for the rich and the powerful, they accused him of madness and lying, and said that his followers were the most vile people.

They tried to bargain with him and asked him to expel the poor believers so that they could sit with him, but Noah strongly refused.

When the people’s harm to Noah and the believers intensified, God revealed to him that none of his people would believe except those who believed.

Then Noah raised his hands in supplication against the unjust people: “My Lord, do not leave on earth homes of the disbelievers.”

God answered his prayer and commanded him to build a huge ship as a means of escape for him and the believers.

Noah began collecting wood and building the ark in a desert place where there was no sea or rivers.

The people were passing by and mocking him, saying: “Oh Noah, did you become a carpenter after you were a prophet? Where will your ship sail in these sands?”

Noah confidently replied to them: “If you mock us, then we will mock you just as you mock.”

After years of hard work, the construction of the great ship was completed, God's command came and signs of torment began to appear.

The oven (bread oven) filled with water, and this was the sign agreed upon between Noah and his Lord.

God commanded Noah to carry in the ark every kind of animal and bird, male and female, to preserve their offspring.

He also ordered him to carry his family and the few believers who had steadfastly with him throughout those centuries.

The sky began to rain with unprecedented intensity, and the ground split open and powerful springs of water gushed out of it.

The water of the sky met the water of the earth, and a great flood was formed that swallowed up villages, cities, trees, and mountains.

In the midst of this terrifying flood, Noah called to his son, who was standing far away with the unbelievers: “My son, ride with us and do not be with the unbelievers.”

The arrogant son replied: “I will go to a mountain that will protect me from the water.”

Noah replied sadly: “Today there is no protector of God’s command except those who have mercy.”

The waves came between them and the son was one of those who drowned, so that God would give an example that the bond of religion and piety is stronger than the bond of blood.

The ship moved under God’s grace in waves like mountains, protecting the believers inside it from the destruction that befell the unbelievers.

After everyone who associated others with God was drowned and the earth was cleansed of corruption, God commanded the sky to uproot and the earth to swallow its water.

The ark settled safely on a mountain called “Al-Judi,” and Noah and the believers landed to begin a new life based on monotheism.

The lesson of the story of Noah, peace be upon him, is great patience in the face of affliction and continuing to call for the truth, no matter the difficulties and ridicule we face.

We also learn that salvation can only be achieved through obedience to God, and that stubbornness and arrogance inevitably lead to clear destruction.
